pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Indiana does not use one single statewide journeyman electrician exam for every candidate. Journeyman electrician licensing, registration, and testing requirements are commonly set by local jurisdictions. A candidate may need to follow the rules of a city, county, municipal licensing board, local building department, or other local authority. A commonly used journeyman-level electrical exam format is the ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam. That exam includes 80 multiple-choice questions, allows 4 hours of testing time, and is open book. Its subject areas include general knowledge, services and service equipment, feeders, branch circuits and conductors, wiring methods and materials, equipment and devices, control devices, motors and generators, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions. The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam places strong emphasis on wiring methods and materials, branch circuits and conductors, equipment and devices, services and service equipment, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates taking that exam may use approved reference materials during the examination, subject to the exam provider’s rules. Because Indiana journeyman electrician testing is commonly controlled at the local level, candidates must follow the exam-room rules for the specific exam they are scheduled to take. Open book testing still requires strong preparation. The National Electrical Code is a detailed technical reference, and a candidate who is unfamiliar with its structure can lose valuable time searching through unrelated articles. A prepared candidate should be able to identify the subject of the question, locate the correct NEC article or table, interpret the wording, and apply the rule accurately. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is intended to help candidates practice code navigation before exam day.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Indiana journeyman electrician licensing steps depend on the local authority that issues or recognizes the credential. A candidate may need to apply through a city licensing office, county department, municipal board, local building department, or electrical licensing authority. Because Indiana does not issue one uniform statewide journeyman electrician license, identifying the correct local jurisdiction is the first step. A typical Indiana journeyman electrician path may include completing supervised electrical work experience, finishing apprenticeship or classroom training when required, gathering employer verification, submitting a local application, paying required local fees, scheduling the approved electrical examination, passing the required exam, and completing any remaining local licensing or registration steps.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Indiana does not have one statewide journeyman electrician license issued to every individual electrician. Electrical licensing, registration, and examination requirements are commonly handled by local governments. Cities, counties, and municipalities may set their own rules for journeyman electricians, electrical contractors, permits, registrations, renewals, and local work authorization. Some employers may also require a journeyman-level credential as part of hiring, promotion, or jobsite qualification standards.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Because Indiana electrical licensing is commonly managed locally, the licensing process begins by identifying the authority that controls electrical licensing in the city, county, or town where the candidate plans to work. This may be a building department, contractor licensing office, board of electrical examiners, municipal licensing department, or other local authority having jurisdiction. After locating the correct authority, candidates should confirm the license classification they need. Depending on the jurisdiction, the credential may be called master electrician, electrical contractor, journeyman electrician, supervising electrician, residential electrician, or municipal electrical registration. Each classification may have its own experience requirements, application steps, exam rules, insurance requirements, bond requirements, renewal requirements, and business registration requirements. The next step is reviewing the application requirements.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Indiana electrical licensing requirements can vary significantly by local jurisdiction. A license or registration accepted in one city or county may not automatically authorize electrical work in another location. Candidates should confirm the rules for the exact area where they plan to perform, supervise, or contract electrical work. Local authorities may set requirements for experience, examination, business registration, insurance, bonding, permits, inspections, continuing education, renewal cycles, and license classification. An individual credential may demonstrate technical qualification, while a contractor license or registration may authorize a business to offer electrical contracting services.
